data.title: Paradise Lost
data.author: adharmad
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在1961年与朋友Sasha Polyakov一同接受Landau的“理论最低考试”的经历。Landau是苏联著名的物理学家，他的考试以其高难度和严苛著称。作者描述了他们被安排在Kapitza物理问题研究所解决数学问题，期间不断受到Landau的严厉批评和嘲讽。尽管感到屈辱，但他们最终通过了考试。作者的父亲，作为Landau的老友，解释说这种严厉其实是一种尊重的表现。Landau还为他们写了推荐信，帮助他们破格参加物理技术学院的入学考试，这在当时是非常难得的。文章还提到Landau去世后，其学生和同事创建了Landau理论物理研究所，对20世纪物理学发展产生了重要影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇关于苏联时期生活和物理学的文章的不同方面的评论

不同观点：
• **lioeters**：对苏联时期（尤其是1970年代）的生活充满怀念。认为当时虽然物质匮乏，但人们生活自由、无忧无虑，举办过许多狂野的派对，充满青春和无拘无束的氛围。他提到当时金钱并不重要，生活中的美好事物似乎是“免费的”。
  
• **ramrunner0xff**：主要关注文章中的物理学内容，特别是高斯随机力和牛顿方程的量子化。他表示对物理见解印象深刻，并计划进一步研究相关内容，同时反思了自己对微分方程的生疏。

• **rml**：欣赏文章的写作风格，表达了对这种类型内容的喜爱，但未具体提及对文章内容（生活或物理学）的看法。

• **trhway**：与lioeters的观点部分相似，也对过去那个充满快乐和自由的时代表示怀念，但同时指出，那些时光已经一去不复返。他还提到俄罗斯的新法律，显示出对当前俄罗斯政治环境（如FSB重新介入科学管理）的担忧，暗示某些过去的特点可能正在回归。

补充讨论：
• **gnabgib**：仅提到年份（2012），未发表具体评论或观点，可能暗示对文章时间背景的关注或提醒其他读者注意文章的时间点。

争议焦点：
• 对苏联时期生活的评价存在一定的情感差异。**lioeters**和**trhway**都怀念过去，但**trhway**对当前局势表现出更多的忧虑，暗示了过去某些负面因素（如政治控制）的回归。
• **ramrunner0xff**和**rml**更关注文章的写作和知识内容，未参与对苏联生活的情感讨论，显示出评论者兴趣点的多样性。

44741314.article_content:
Talk at Mitchell Feigenbaum Conference
Lev Landau
The initiation into Landau School of Thought started with famous Theoretical Minimum Exam. This was a sequence of increasing tests of that rare mix of knowledge, durability and passion, which was necessary to be accepted and survive the School.
I was lucky to be initiated by Landau himself, just one year before the tragic automobile accident, after which Landau never recovered. My friend Sasha Polyakov and I came to Landau in spring of 1961, with zero combined life experience and infinite combined self-confidence, after some success in Mathematical Olympics where we shared the First Prize.
Landau had that childish expression at his face — a mixture of surprise, impatience and arrogance — as if he was saying: “Let us see if you are as dumb as I think you are.”
Kapitza Institute in Moscow
He placed us in two different offices in “Kapichnik” (Kapitza Institute for Physical Problems), gave us some math problems and started pacing between these offices, looking over our shoulders with curiosity and making nasty remarks at every line we wrote.
I felt as if my Lord came to Earth and crucified me with His own hands. One of my problems was to integrate rational function—textbooks recommend the method of variation of constants — i.e. to represent
,
with a being roots of
, and obtain coefficients c as residues at x=a and similarly for coefficients of polynomial
as residues at
.
But I have never read those textbooks — in fact I was very bad at reading textbooks all my life — I preferred to do it myself and then ask my educated friends whether my solution was right.
I had just a few minutes to invent my own method before Dau would have run out of his short patience. I do not remember now how I solved that problem — but I remember very well that I did, because I still hear his voice in my head — “Well, you finally got a solution — invented a wheel — should have known such triviality in a first place”.
Sashka had similar experience in his cell, after which we were pulled together in Dau’s office and he looked into our eyes without smiling. “Well, kids — you passed, but you got to really work on your mathematical skills — theoretician cannot live with the skills like that. You got to know Complex Analysis, PDE, Group Theory, all nice and easy stuff — and everything else they will teach you in the University you just flow around (“obtekaite”).”
Arkady Migdal and Sasha Migdal, the early 60′s
I came back home totally humiliated. My father Arkady, former student, friend and rival of Landau, was waiting for me. He was initiated in the thirties without even being tested by TheorMinimum.
“Congratulations—you passed the first Landau Exam” — he hugged me, but I pushed back. “What are you talking about? Landau was cursing us, he said that a theoretician cannot live with the technique like that, he was mocking the way we solved problems…”
“He showed his respect to you idiots by treating 15-year old boys as grown-up theoreticians! Do you really think the grown-up theoretician could live with your mathematical technique? Go and learn Group Theory like he suggested, and always take good advice regardless how insulting it may sound! … And by the way, he called me up right after you two left his office and he was very excited. He said that you were so smart, you reminded him of himself when he was young.”
Landau did more than that to help us. He wrote a letter, recommending us to be accepted in the University, which later actually helped that miracle to happen. There were two miracles, in fact. One, young kids were allowed to attend the Physical Technical Institute entrance exams without graduating from high school. Second, Jews were actually accepted into PhysTech, which was next to impossible.
Sasha Polyakov, Vitya Zharinov, Seriozha Gurvitz, and Sasha Migdal in the mid-60s at Military Training
The Landau letter was so good, that it was never shown to us, until just a few years ago. We lived in tough country at tough times, when kids were not supposed to be spoiled by being praised. I guess now this letter cannot spoil us anymore.
After Landau’s death Isaak Khalatnikov and few other Apostles created the Landau Institute of Theoretical Physics. It was late sixties, when the Stalin’s Fear was starting to fade, and Iron Curtain was starting to rust a little. KGB still ruled the country, but it was already playing more sophisticated games, not necessarily the deadly ones.
Isaak Khalatnikov is truly a remarkable man, whose immense contribution to Theoretical Physics is underestimated in my view. He was involved in seminal work with Landau and Abrikosov, where they first discovered the famous “zero charge” problem, and laid the ground for a modern quest for consistent filed theory. But his life achievement is creation and leadership of Landau Institute, which played such an important role in History of Physics of the 20th Century.
Landau with his Apostles. First row, right to left: E. Lifshitz
44741314.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在1961年与朋友Sasha Polyakov一同接受Landau的“理论最低考试”的经历。Landau是苏联著名的物理学家，他的考试以其高难度和严苛著称。作者描述了他们被安排在Kapitza物理问题研究所解决数学问题，期间不断受到Landau的严厉批评和嘲讽。尽管感到屈辱，但他们最终通过了考试。作者的父亲，作为Landau的老友，解释说这种严厉其实是一种尊重的表现。Landau还为他们写了推荐信，帮助他们破格参加物理技术学院的入学考试，这在当时是非常难得的。文章还提到Landau去世后，其学生和同事创建了Landau理论物理研究所，对20世纪物理学发展产生了重要影响。

How the Kyiv Independent reached 20,000 paying members — with no paywall
Horizontal connections and membership community have kept subscriber churn for the English-language publication under 2%.
By
Sarah Scire
@SarahScire
July 28, 2025, 2:20 p.m.
July 28, 2025, 2:20 p.m.
The Kyiv Independent reached a major membership milestone last month with a global campaign telling readers “journalism needs a community, not a paywall.”
After a month-long multi-country campaign, The Kyiv Independent has more than 20,000 paying members — up from 17,500 in May. Most members give $5 a month. About 70% of the outlet’s revenue is from readers.
The Kyiv Independent was co-founded in November 2021 by a group of journalists who’d been fired from the Kyiv Post — the biggest English-language newspaper in the country — as the owner attempted to interfere in the newsroom. (The staff has grown from 18 in 2021 to
70 today, including more than 40 in the newsroom
.) The Kyiv Independent tells readers it was “born out of a fight for freedom of speech” and has not shied away from honestly appraising Ukraine’s leadership during war. Just last week, the site was
targeted by a DDoS attack
after publishing
coverage
and
sharp criticism
of the government’s anti-corruption rollback.
The digital news outlet also gets revenue from a thriving online store selling items like
a print magazine
and
Borshch tote bag
, content syndication, advertising, and one-time donations from individuals and organizations such as Microsoft and UNESCO.
Importantly, paid members are sticking around. The Kyiv Independent has a monthly churn rate of less than 2%, growth membership manager
Yana Zhuryk
said. (For context: The
average monthly churn
for a median news outlet is 3.6%, according to INMA, meaning 67% of new subscribers stay for a year and 28% stick around for three years.)
Many readers are interested in the organization itself — a combination of a startup journey and a newsroom living through a war. The Kyiv Independent sends weekly behind-the-scenes missives (on topics like how journalists keep working through air raids) to members. The growing membership team has also achieved near-superhuman levels of responsiveness.
“We give them a lot of human connection,” Kyiv Independent COO
Zakhar Protsiuk
said. “Everyone who becomes a member, if they reach out to us in any form, anywhere, we have a one-on-one communication with them — whether that’s through email, Discord, meetings. We answer every single letter we receive, even replies to, like, our email marketing.”
RELATED ARTICLE
“Politics as a chronic stressor”: News about politics bums you out and can make you feel ill — but it also makes you take action
Joshua Benton
September 21, 2020
But Protsiuk sees horizontal connections —
between
members, rather than from newsroom to audience — as possibly more important to the model’s success. The Kyiv Independent connects readers to each other through monthly events, its Discord, community maps, Ukrainian lessons with a language tutor, and localized campaigns. More than a third of its members
pinned their location on the outlet’s community map
and about 10% of its most-engaged members are active on the Discord, he said.
Almost all (about 95%) of Kyiv Independent’s paid members live outside Ukraine — with countries like the United States (accounting for about 40% of paid members), Canada, the U.K., Nordic countries, France, and Germany well-represented. A lot of the membership connections, then, happen online.
“It’s a very geographically widespread audience. Members develop an interest and understanding of what’s happening in Ukraine for different reasons. Some might have some personal connection. Others got interested during the full-scale war,” Protsiuk said. “Those segments are very different, but I think for many of them, since the international attention to Ukraine has [gotten] lower, they often don’t feel the same connection. Like, they think about this topic quite a lot, and their friends don’t. Once they become a member, we create this horizontal connection for them to feel like they have other people to discuss this [with].”
The Kyiv Independent deployed some country-specific messaging in its campaign. In Denmark, it congratulated readers for making Denmark the No. 1 country in the world in terms of paid members per capita. (“The Danes liked that.”) It also introduced some friendly competition. In Sweden, the outlet told readers Denmark was No. 1, inviting Swedish readers to step up and take the top spot.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta公司及其CEO马克关于超级智能和未来技术的愿景

不同观点：
• **对超级智能愿景的质疑**：
  - [hnthrow90348765] 认为马克的声明只是为了显示自己没有意图带来反乌托邦，但实际并未提出有效方案。他建议Meta转为非营利组织以增加可信度。
  - [DanHulton] 通过比喻指出，马克将工具的逐步改进误认为最终会变成完全不同的工具（超级智能），这种推论是荒谬的。
  - [jameskilton] 批评马克没有从过去的错误中学习，并认为Meta的超级智能愿景不会带来任何好处。

• **对Meta公司动机的怀疑**：
  - [Voloskaya] 质疑Meta在开源和风险控制方面的立场，认为其转向封闭源代码是出于竞争考虑而非风险管理。
  - [mrcwinn] 和 [adrianbooth17] 都提到Meta的商业模式依赖于数据提取和行为操控，因此对其“个人超级智能”的概念持怀疑态度。
  - [aeon_ai] 回顾Meta的历史，指出其平台已经因为追求利益而忽视了对社会的伤害，因此对其未来的超级智能愿景不信任。

• **对超级智能潜在影响的担忧**：
  - [osti] 和 [aschobel] 关注超级智能可能带来的安全问题以及Meta对开源的潜在放弃。
  - [amradio1989] 担心“个人超级智能”会如何处理和使用用户的私人数据。

• **对超级智能愿景的支持**：
  - [tim333] 持相对积极的态度，认为超级智能是未来的趋势，尽管不确定Meta是否是实现这一目标的最佳公司。

补充讨论：
• **技术进步对社会的影响**：
  - [Voloskaya] 质疑技术进步是否真的让人类有更多时间投入创造力、文化、关系和享受生活，认为这种说法缺乏依据。
  - [twoodfin] 对马克关于生产力软件和劳动的未来影响的观点提出疑问，认为其描述不够准确。

• **对Meta公司历史的批评**：
  - [subpixel] 通过个人在FB市场上的体验质疑Meta的实际能力。
  - [azinman2] 总结了对Meta愿景的全面怀疑，认为Meta过去的行为使其未来更强大的技术带来的影响令人担忧。

争议焦点：
• 马克关于超级智能的愿景是否可信以及Meta是否具备实现这一愿景的道德和技术能力。
• Meta是否会因为商业利益而放弃开源和风险管理。
• 超级智能对个人隐私和数据安全的潜在威胁。

data.title: Show HN: AgentGuard – Auto-kill AI agents before they burn through your budget
data.author: dipampaul17
data.article_summary: AgentGuard是一个实时保护工具，旨在防止AI代理在工作流中出现无限循环和超支问题。它通过监控AI的API调用并实时跟踪成本，当达到预设预算限制时自动终止进程，避免开发者因错误或无限循环而导致高额费用。与其他工具相比，AgentGuard能在代码执行过程中实时阻止超支，而不仅是事后报告。使用方式简单，只需在代码中添加两行，设置预算限制即可。AgentGuard提供多种保护模式，包括抛出可恢复错误、警告通知和强制终止，帮助开发者有效控制成本。

data.author: amrrs

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI在挪威建设AI设施的计划及其相关影响

不同观点：
• 支持观点：
   - [jtrn]: 作为挪威人，对该项目充满希望，期待其在Narvik的落地，认为该地有丰富的可再生能源和良好的冷却条件，适合数据中心建设。同时，对AI技术充满热情，尽管认识到需要控制对技术的过度乐观。
   - [pu_pe]: 强调该项目的规模庞大，与丹麦的超级计算机相比具有显著优势，显示出对项目前景的乐观态度。

• 反对观点：
   - [danielscrubs]: 对OpenAI与挪威政府的合作持怀疑态度，担心ChatGPT可能被用作转移石油财富的工具，暗示对大公司的不信任。
   - [roschdal]: 明确表示不欢迎OpenAI的Stargate项目，要求其离开。

• 经济与技术考量：
   - [londons_explore]: 指出AI数据中心选址的经济性变化，认为在电力便宜和自然冷却条件好的地方（如冰岛）建数据中心更具优势。
   - [speedgoose]: 预测挪威北部将因该项目面临电价上涨的问题，类似挪威南部已经经历的情况。
   - [astahlx]: 质疑选择挪威的原因，认为应选择易于快速建设新电厂且靠近数据中心的国家。

• 娱乐与文化参考：
   - [atleastoptimal]: 提到Pantheon电视系列，暗示可能与AI相关。
   - [sexeriy237]: 幽默地指出，如果该项目不涉及Stargate或类似科幻概念，就不应以此命名。

• 媒体与外部链接：
   - [vintermann]: 提到挪威新闻将该设施误认为是半导体制造厂。
   - [lelanthran]: 提供了一个外部链接，讨论项目的可行性问题。

• 个人影响与担忧：
   - [Y-bar]: 担心该项目将成为主要电力买家，导致未来冬季电费上涨。
   - [mutkach]: 对比之前宣传的规模，认为该项目的230MW较小，并质疑是否为之前传闻中的"Stargate"项目。

补充讨论：
• 项目选址的合理性与对当地经济、能源的影响是讨论的核心。
• 对AI技术的态度呈现两极化，有人热情支持，有人强烈反对。
• 挪威当地居民对该项目的复杂情感，包括对潜在经济利益的期待和对生活成本上升的担忧。
• 对OpenAI公司战略和命名方式的幽默与讽刺。

data.title: Tracking source locations in the Futhark compiler
data.author: jmillikin
data.article_summary: Futhark是一种高性能的纯函数式并行数组编程语言。为了帮助程序员优化程序速度，Futhark引入了性能分析工具。最初，Futhark只支持转储GPU操作报告，后来增加了`futhark profile`命令，可以将基准测试生成的机器可读数据转化为人类可读的报告。报告显示了各个成本中心的执行时间，如GPU内核和数据拷贝操作。然而，报告中的名称是编译器生成的，可能不易直接对应到源代码中的函数，特别是由于内联和优化导致的关系模糊。例如，"segmap"和"scan"操作可能对应于多个嵌套的扫描操作。通过这些工具，程序员可以更好地理解和优化程序性能。

Tracking source locations
Posted on July 29, 2025
Futhark is a programming language meant for writing fast programs, but as is the
case for every programming language meant for writing fast programs, it
inevitably happens that a programmer will use it to write a program that is not
fast. When this happens, the programmer will likely want to know why their
program is not fast, and how to make it faster. A useful tool for answering such
questions is a
profiler
- a tool that tells you how long the different parts
of your program take to run. This post is about how profiling in Futhark became
slightly more useful with the
most recent
release
.
Initially, Futhark had no real profiling support, except for some
semi-documented support for dumping a report of GPU operations. Eventually we
added
futhark profile
,
which allows the machine-readable profiling data produced by
futhark bench
to be
turned into human-readable reports. Specifically, the Futhark runtime system
will tally up the time spent in various cost centres, which for the GPU backends
are GPU kernels and other operations such as copies, and put it in a table.

Now a user may reasonable object:
âHold on! I donât remember
my
program
containing anything called
main.segmap_23494
!â
And indeed, these cost centres
refer to compiler-generated names. You can squint to get
some
meaning out of
them:
segscan
is certainly some kind of
scan
operation, and
segmap
is a
map
. But due to inlining, it can be difficult to guess which functions result
in which GPU operations, and optimisations may obscure the relation between
source code and generated code - indeed, those
segmap_intrablock
operations
are actually mainly (nested)
scan
s that are then turned into block-level scans
via
incremental
flattening
.
44742359.article_summary: Futhark是一种高性能的纯函数式并行数组编程语言。为了帮助程序员优化程序速度，Futhark引入了性能分析工具。最初，Futhark只支持转储GPU操作报告，后来增加了`futhark profile`命令，可以将基准测试生成的机器可读数据转化为人类可读的报告。报告显示了各个成本中心的执行时间，如GPU内核和数据拷贝操作。然而，报告中的名称是编译器生成的，可能不易直接对应到源代码中的函数，特别是由于内联和优化导致的关系模糊。例如，"segmap"和"scan"操作可能对应于多个嵌套的扫描操作。通过这些工具，程序员可以更好地理解和优化程序性能。

data.title: You know what: Microsoft became miserably incompetent in IT
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者作为开源软件开发者，在使用微软邮件服务时遇到的问题。作者试图发送一封包含多个链接的邮件到LibreOffice开发邮件列表，但邮件未能发送，随后其微软账户被封锁。作者尝试通过申诉恢复账户，但遇到自动化回复和无效的解决方案，最终在一周后在他人帮助下才恢复访问。作者认为微软作为曾经的IT技术领导者，如今在技术支持和产品质量上表现出严重的无能，对此感到失望。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [burnt-resistor] 认为技术不完美可以接受，但如果没有良好的客户支持，小问题可能演变为阻碍用户继续使用的大问题。他以Meta为例，说明即使技术有缺陷，良好的支持可以解决问题。

44741442.article_content:
You know what: Microsoft became miserably incompetent in IT.
I develop open-source code. But that never made me one of the “I hate proprietary software or IT giant corporations” types. I always saw the nice things that Microsoft offered to its users; I saw not only downsides in its products. And I also used (and continue to use) things created by it: Windows to start with (and I develop there, being able to debug and address issues specific to the platform that most of our users use); but also its email service for personal mail.
This Monday, I decided to send something to LibreOffice dev mailing list. Something I do from time to time, you know. Not too fascinating, right?
Well, this time, it turned out, Microsoft decided to teach me to fear them. Thunderbird shown me a message, that the mail couldn’t be sent (well, not a problem: will re-try again…), but then I found myself logged off, with “Your account has been blocked” message. They decided, that I violated
their service agreement
!
FTR:
here is the mail
. I was able to send it using another tech giant’s mail service. You may see that it’s full of links. Yes, that’s true; I prefer to provide references to my words. But tell me where was it violating anything in MS agreement?
OK, they have a stupid AI that is worse than good old filters. OK, they made it react immediately, as an undoubted authority. But that’s not a big problem, right? They provide a way to appeal! Let me do that.
And of course, they ask for the phone, and I provide it, just to get a nice reply:
And guess what: there is
no other method
!
OK! Let’s ask their support. (I am approaching to the point that fascinated me most.) I found a link to “Contact Microsoft Support” on the “Troubleshooting verification code issues” page; and after some automatic answers there, which didn’t answer my problem, I finally got a button telling me … tada …
Yes, you got it right. “Here is a page where we discuss problems signing in. You attempted our FAQ suggestions? You still can’t sign in? No problem! Contact our Support team, and we will solve your problem is a minute! But first, please sign in to continue.”
Heh. I used my wife’s account to contact support. And then I was given a very secret link to an appeal form, where I could file a support ticket. And the next morning, I got a message! Yay! It told me to do something! Let me try! What is that they tell me to do? Reading… hmm… go to sign-in page, and when they tell me that my account is blocked, provide a phone number? Wasn’t it exactly the thing I attempted and failed, and told them about that? But hey, they obviously fixed that problem overnight, they couldn’t just send me the useless instructions, right? Or could they?
They could.
They just ignored my description. They repeated the useless instructions, without taking care to check what the problem was. And they closed the ticket automatically. It has been resolved, you know.
I still am in the process. I filed another ticket, which they didn’t care to answer. I am still hopeful.
But this, once an IT tech leader, became utterly incompetent in IT. And for me, it’s a pity.

data.title: Open source BOM management (for me)
data.author: vincent-uden
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了一位嵌入式软件开发者在转向硬件设计（PCB设计）过程中遇到的组件管理问题及解决方案。起初，作者通过模块化和简化设计原则（如DRY和KISS）成功设计了电路，但随着使用多达40种不同组件的电路板增多，组件库存管理变得混乱。为解决这一问题，作者开发了一个开源的BOM（物料清单）管理工具，结合Gridfinity网格存储系统，利用3D打印的网格收纳盒管理组件。该工具通过可视化界面展示组件位置，支持从Altium Designer导入BOM，并能批量管理库存。未来，作者计划增加BOM批量采购导出功能和网格布局自定义等功能，以进一步提升工具的实用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子元件存储和管理系统的优化和功能建议

不同观点：
• **jpatten** 认为目前最挑战的问题是保持元件数量的更新。他建议增加一个功能，可以输入“制作了25个模块”，系统自动扣除各个元件的数量，并考虑增加一个额外百分比来应对像0402这样的小元件容易丢失的情况。他还进一步设想了一个功能，可以解析DigiKey/Mouser等订单或者读取包装袋上的条形码来自动更新数量，并考虑如何支持不同的存储方式，比如卷盘存储。

• **Robelius** 关注的是网格高亮系统，特别是在网格中存放超过49种不同元件时的处理方式。他提出了是否允许一个立方体中存放多种不同元件的问题，并询问是否更倾向于将同类元件混合存放，还是将不同类型的元件混合存放。他提到自己尝试过两种方法，但在没有适当维护的情况下都会出现问题。

• **mycatisblack** 对使用Google表格来映射小元件抽屉网格的方式表示赞同，并表示愿意尝试新的软件。他还提供了一个实际的存储建议，即使用塑料小瓶来存放SMD电阻和电容，并通过在厚塑料板上钻孔来排列这些小瓶，从而在一个抽屉中存放更多元件。

补充讨论：
• **jpatten** 强调了自动化和精确管理元件数量的重要性，特别是对于大规模生产和小元件容易丢失的情况。
• **Robelius** 则更关注存储系统的灵活性和可维护性，尤其是在元件种类繁多的情况下如何有效地组织和管理。
• **mycatisblack** 提供了一种具体的、低成本的物理存储解决方案，并分享了实际操作中的经验。

争议焦点：
• **Robelius** 提出的关于网格系统中多于49种元件的处理问题，以及元件混合存放的偏好问题，可能在实际应用中引起不同用户的争议，因为这涉及到个人或团队的工作习惯和存储策略。

总结：讨论主要围绕电子元件存储系统的功能改进和物理存储方案的实际应用展开，涉及自动更新数量的功能需求和不同存储方式的优劣比较。

44703581.article_content:
Open source BOM management
July 2025
20:20
Since graduating from university Iâve gotten more and more into embedded software development. This has even spilled over into designing PCBs
(printed circuit boards)
for my embedded devices to sit on.
Initially I had assumed that the leap from software to hardware design would be insurmountable without any formal education but it turned out to be quite enjoyable. It turned out that the problem Iâd be facing wasnât a technical one, but of an organisational nature.
Designing circuits
Designing circuits turned out to be a lot like software development. Or at least I managed to force it to become similar to how I develop software.
Modular parts or blocks, which I could share between circuits needing similar functionality sounds a lot like
DRY
. Avoiding complexity by only including the absolute bare minimum that I could get away with sure sounds like
KISS
. And so I charged forwards into the world of power electronics, sensors and Bluetooth communication, armed to the teeth with sort-of applicable design principles.
I ordered PCBs, parts and went to town with soldering paste, stencils and a soldering iron to realise my new creations. And that is where the problems began.
Parts and components
Each circuit could be composed of up to ~40 different parts that needed to be mounted on the board. And since I had been so clever as to share designs between boards I could even use parts from the stocks of one circuit board to build another design if it was missing any parts.
One day, when I was looking to build
Battery manager V1.2
and was scrambling through box after box of components I realised that I couldnât find the appropriate step-down converters needed. In fact, I didnât even know if I had any left. And for that matter, did I have any 10 kÎ© resistors left?
The overlapping component usage had left me with no actual idea of my inventory. There was no way of knowing how many of each circuit design that I could actually build and ordering new parts was just as big of a nightmare since couldnât get a grip on what parts Iâd actually need.
Keeping stock of components for my designs was a new problem I hadnât considered. If I want to build a version of my latest pdf-reader on a new computer, I just compile it. Thereâs no need to check for complex, interwoven dependencies between it and other software Iâd written before constructing the design, in software you can just do it.
The solution
Having the hammer of software development at my disposal, organising electrical components was looking a lot like a nail. The resulting program consists of parts, a panel and a grid.
As the mouse hovers over each electrical part, itâs position in the grid is highlighted on the right.
Why a grid? What does it represent?
A physical, 3D-printed grid storage system of course.
The grid is part of the modular, open-source storage system
Gridfinity
. In particular the parts I used were generated in the OpenSCAD-powered
Gridfinity Generator
.
This parametric interface allowed be to print bins for each component and a compatible baseplate for them to stand on. Among other models it also allowed me to generate
.stl
files for a portable carrying box (
Rugged box
) which I use to transport the parts from my cabinet to the electronics lab for assembly.
Bins
As could probably be derived from the mixed colouring of my grid, I printed the parts from filament I had laying around, thus the slightly stochastic look.
To label each bin I wrote a
typst
file which automatically lays out each component name on an A4 paper with guides for where to cut. The only input is a list of component names whose labels shall be printed
#let names = (
"ERF1002",
"TMK107B7105KA-T",
"STPS1H100A",
"105017-0001",
"...",
)
ECAD to BOM
Having a mapping from a physical grid of components to a digital database of their count seems useful but isnât enough to provide a satisfactory user experience.
The most important part of the software isnât visible until the left panel is switch from
Part Search
to
BOM Search
. In BOM (
bill of materials
) mode, I can search for entire sets of parts belonging to circuits Iâve designed. These are of course imported straight from the
csv
export of
Altium Designer
where I design them.
Opening a BOM shows the location of all components needed to assemble it and allows for batch stock management. This shows me which bins to place in the aforementioned rugged box to be brought to assembly.
Future work
While the software is currently perfectly usable, I should know since I use it frequently, there is still room for improvement. Key features Iâm looking to implement in the future are:
BOM export for bulk purchases at Digi-Key or Mouser
Settings for the grid, not everyone (or me in the future) is going to have a 7x7 grid layout
Grid-based search. Right now the search is one way, from the left panel to the grid. A user should be able to query the grid for the component it is supposed

补充讨论：
• **jpatten** 强调了自动化和精确管理元件数量的重要性，特别是对于大规模生产和小元件容易丢失的情况。
• **Robelius** 则更关注存储系统的灵活性和可维护性，尤其是在元件种类繁多的情况下如何有效地组织和管理。
• **mycatisblack** 提供了一种具体的、低成本的物理存储解决方案，并分享了实际操作中的经验。

争议焦点：
• **Robelius** 提出的关于网格系统中多于49种元件的处理问题，以及元件混合存放的偏好问题，可能在实际应用中引起不同用户的争议，因为这涉及到个人或团队的工作习惯和存储策略。

总结：讨论主要围绕电子元件存储系统的功能改进和物理存储方案的实际应用展开，涉及自动更新数量的功能需求和不同存储方式的优劣比较。

data.title: Friction and Not Being Touched
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了现代人工智能（AI）系统被描绘成“万能机器”（Everything Machines）的现象。这些系统被宣传为能解决一切问题，无论失败都是因为使用不当或技术不足，而不是系统本身的局限性。这种观点脱离了AI实际能力的物理和技术现实。同时，文章探讨了“无摩擦性”（frictionlessness）的概念，在科技领域，无摩擦通常被视为理想状态，但作者认为摩擦在社会和认知层面有重要作用。摩擦让我们感受到他人的存在、观点和需求，是社会互动的一部分。无摩擦性则体现了自我的、孤立的心态，让人不必承认或接触他人。AI作为万能机器的叙事本质上反映了这种不愿被他人“触碰”的心态，避免了人与人之间的互动和必要的摩擦，最终可能导致个体与社会的隔离。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“无摩擦体验”的争议及其在不同情境下的意义和影响

不同观点：
• [nmeofthestate] 认为该讨论毫无价值，完全是浪费时间，没有具体展开论据。
• [camgunz] 持相对积极的态度，提到Trevor Noah和Esther Perel的相关讨论，认为视频内容既有娱乐性又有知识性，支持无摩擦体验的潜在好处。
• [atoav] 反对作者对无摩擦的推崇，认为摩擦是组织和系统中不可或缺的一部分。他以客户服务和税务表格为例，指出摩擦有时是系统设计的必要部分，可以过滤掉不必要的需求。他还提到，现实中某些流程本身具有摩擦，如果隐瞒这种摩擦，反而是对用户的误导。
• [elcapitan] 对原文中“无摩擦带有自恋倾向”的观点提出异议，认为强迫他人与自己互动反而是更自恋的行为，支持在某些情况下无摩擦体验的合理性。
• [throw839340949r] 强烈反对原文作者的观点，认为人们选择无摩擦体验并非出于情感需求或寻求安全空间，而是因为有更重要的事情要做。他还提到保持个人空间的重要性，并以疾病和过敏为例，认为避免身体接触是合理的，不应被视为孤僻或逃避。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是无摩擦体验是否必然带有自恋或孤僻的倾向。部分评论者如[elcapitan]和[throw839340949r]认为这种观点是对无摩擦体验的误解和偏见。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是摩擦在系统设计中的必要性。[atoav]详细阐述了摩擦在过滤需求和管理复杂流程中的作用，并指出某些情况下摩擦是不可避免的。
• [camgunz]提供的视频链接为讨论提供了另一种视角，展示了无摩擦体验在某些情境下的潜在优势和吸引力。
• 个人空间和身体接触的问题在讨论中也占据了一定篇幅，[throw839340949r]以疾病和过敏为例，强调保护个人空间和避免接触的合理性。

总结：评论中对“无摩擦体验”的态度存在明显分歧，部分人支持其潜在优势，另一部分人则强调摩擦在现实系统设计中的必要性和合理性，同时讨论还涉及个人空间和身体接触的问题。

44742021.article_content:
Friction and not being touched
Jul 30, 2025
—
by
tante
in
english
,
Writing
The journalist Karen Hao – who published an absolutely fantastic book about OpenAI called “
Empire of AI
” recently – coined (as far as I know) one of the best terms for describing modern “AI” systems:
Everything Machines
.
“AI” systems are not framed as
specific tools
that solve specific problems in specific ways but just as solution in itself: There is nothing “AI” cannot do, if it fails we just failed it by not prompting it right or not building large enough data centers or not waiting for another 6 months when these stochastic systems will totally be able to do whatever was needed. Pinky swear.
This trick disconnects the physical and technical realities of the capabilities and lack thereof of connectivist “AI” systems built on stochastic correlations between patterns in data and what these systems are
narratively positioned
to be able to do. LLMs cannot really do people’s jobs – they might be able to kinda do very small parts, especially if quality is not a criterium – but they are always presented as such: Whether it’s by doomers who predict massive unemployment and poverty or by apologists who predict an age of leisure. The Everything Machine can do – as the name implies – everything. Solve everything.
Lately I’ve been thinking about friction a lot. Not the physical force that allows us to walk and all that – even though that also is neat – but cognitive and social friction and its function.
In tech circles friction is seen as bad, everything needs to be friction
less
. Every interaction with anything needs to be smooth and uninterrupted. Which usually means the path to you parting with your money/attention needs to be as seamless as possible. It’s the logic of casinos: Don’t let gamblers see natural light or a clock so nothing disturbs the efficient process of moving money from a bunch of people to the casino owner.
But it’s not only nefarious reasons that make people design frictionlessness:
Errorless learning
for example wants to remove the friction that making a mistake and being corrected creates in the hope of generating better outcomes. (It’s not a coincidence though, that specifically B. F. Skinner – known for inventing “Skinner Boxes” which is the theory that a lot of modern game and app design is based on to keep people hooked – is a big intellectual force in that space.) Friction can be annoying. Don’t we all just want things to work?
Sure. But friction is not just “things not working properly”, it can also be read as
being touched
. Just as crowded spaces create friction by other people being in my way while moving, a process with friction makes me feel other people’s work, their point of view and how it differs from mine, makes me feel their needs and wants. Friction is part of what being in, being part of society
is
.
The idea of frictionlessness has very narcissistic, “
player character
” vibes: You don’t experience friction if the whole world is build around you and your needs. When you get whatever you want when you want it. That is the Utopia of Frictionlessness: To never be touched by anyone or anything really. Because being actually touched, being inconvenienced, being emotionally moved, having your mind and perception changed means acknowledging your fellow human beings around you, realizing their differences to you and to recognize their value. It means seeing others to a certain degree as your equal. You might be richer, more influential, but we all have bodies that take up space for example. No matter how rich you are, when we all need to share space everyone will take up some.
But especially if you are rich, you can change the equation. You can pay people to keep others away from you. Keep “your space” protected. Can get your demands met at any time. Can influence politics in your favour – which is how we end up not taxing the super rich, casting our societies into socially, economically and politically destructive inequality. Frictionlessness is individualistic and isolating, about disconnecting from the world in any way that does not cater to
your
specific need and want and demand.
And this brings me back to “AI” as Everything Machines. Because that narrative (and the technologies that are deployed under that concept) are basically the crystallization of never having to be touched.
If “AI” solves everything, can do everything you never have to acknowledge anyone else ever again. You never have to think about how we can change our mode of being in this world in a way that is sustainable for this planet and its ecosystem. You never have to think about how to talk to this other person that you need something from.
Modern “AI” systems are sycophantic. Their conversational mode, their mode of interaction is based on frictionlessness. On keeping the conversation going regardless of what’s being said or its meaning or truth even. When interacting with an “AI” system you get to feel to be the only person tha

data.title: I know when you're vibe coding
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者对使用LLM（如AI代码生成工具）编写代码的看法。作者强调，他们不在意代码是如何进入IDE的，无论是手写、复制还是AI生成，关键在于最终合并到代码库的质量。作者指出，虽然LLM生成的代码能正常工作，且清晰可维护，但往往不符合团队的惯例和标准，例如使用不必要的工具或方法。作者担忧开发者为了追求速度而忽视软件开发的基本原则，导致长期可维护性问题。文章最后呼吁开发者关注代码质量和一致性，合理使用LLM，遵循已有原则，而不仅是快速生产原型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在软件开发中的应用及其带来的争议和挑战

不同观点：
• 一些开发者（如lmm）认为，使用LLM可能会导致开发人员采取不够严谨的编码方式，比如在没有充分考虑项目需求和现有模块的情况下编写代码。lmm指出，很多人确实会犯这些错误，而不是像某些人认为的那样遵循最佳实践。
• buserror和bubblyworld则持相对乐观的态度。buserror将LLM视为一个非常初级的程序员，需要大量的指导和审查，但仍然能显著提高工作效率。bubblyworld则认为，AI工具只是工具，问题本质上与人类初级开发者带来的问题相似，可以通过更多的指导来解决。
• palata和agile-gift0262担心LLM会加速不良代码的生产，尤其是对于经验不足的开发者。他们认为，虽然LLM能加快编码速度，但可能导致代码质量下降，增加审查和调试的时间。
• 另一派观点（如clauderoux）则力挺LLM，认为其生成的代码在文档化和可读性方面往往优于人类程序员，且解释详细，能显著提高理解代码的效率。

补充讨论：
• grim_io和nojs提到，许多问题源于过时的AI辅助实践和不充分的上下文工程。他们认为，通过构建更好的项目文档和上下文，可以大幅提高LLM的表现。
• subarctic和atleastoptimal建议，使用LLM时应结合严格的代码检查工具（如linter和formatter），以确保代码风格和行为的正确性。他们还提到，LLM正不断进化，未来可能在更多任务上超越人类程序员。
• Zanfa指出，LLM需要考虑代码库的历史提交，而不仅仅是当前状态，因为许多项目都有从旧模式迁移到新模式的过程。
• 最后，philipp-gayret和nesk_强调，现有的AI工具已经提供了避免这些问题的机制和方法，但需要开发者投入时间去学习和使用。同时，仍需关注软件的实际构建，而不仅仅是原型设计。

争议焦点：
• LLM在软件开发中的实际效果和影响，尤其是在代码质量和开发效率方面的权衡。一方认为LLM会带来更多的不良代码和长期问题，另一方则认为其能提高代码的可读性和开发效率。

44742251.article_content:
I Know When You're Vibe Coding
3
minute read
I shouldn’t have to care about this. I don’t want to care about how someone’s code gets into the IDE. Whether you wrote it by hand, copied it from a forum, prompted an LLM, or ran a simulation where monkeys are given infinite time to produce the solution.
I care about what gets merged into the codebase.
When I click that “Approve” button, I’ve got only a few worries on my mind. Does it produce the correct outcome? Will people understand this next quarter? Will they be able to change it?
But lately, I started noticing things that immediately tell me the code is written by an LLM. No, I don’t mean the repetitive comments (I’m fine with those), not even the switch statements they’re so fond of.
I know the code was generated because it was written in a way no developer on the team would.
It works, it’s clear, it’s tested, and it’s maintainable. But it’s written in a way that doesn’t follow the project conventions we’ve accepted. I know it wasn’t written by a human.
The smell of vibe coding
Because no one would write an HTTP fetching implementation covering all edge cases when we have a data fetching library in the project that already does that.
No one would implement a bunch of utility functions that we already have in a different module.
No one would change a global configuration when there’s a mechanism to do it on a module level.
No one would write a class when we’re using a functional approach everywhere.
I don’t want to know how you wrote this. I just want to know that you care about what comes out of the model. This is code you wouldn’t have produced a couple of years ago.
We spent decades coming up with patterns and standards that help us build maintainable software.
That’s always been the challenge - putting something in production that you can take care of for years. Anyone can vomit up a working implementation. You’ll stitch together a Frankenstein-monster-looking piece of code that will get the job done.
The part we’ve struggled with is making changes to that after you push it out the door.
Is speed the greatest virtue?
I was at a local café a few days ago, and they were training a new barista. There was a long line, and the new guy was startled, rushing to make the next cup, spilling coffee and milk.
We’re back at this stage, rushing to push out the next piece of software because we think that speed is the greatest virtue.
But people want a good cup of coffee, even if they have to wait a little bit for it.
I always thought I’d be getting angry at the finance people who’ll be looking for ways to write smaller digits in the spreadsheets, but I’m disappointed by my fellow developers who quickly threw all principles out of the window so they can speedrun software development.
What I really want
I don’t care how the code got in your IDE.
I want you to care.
I want people to care about quality, I want them to care about consistency, I want them to care about the long-term effects of their work. LLMs are engineering marvels, and I have the utmost respect for the people who’ve created them. But we still need to build software, not productionize prototypes.
Write better prompts. Give better descriptions. Tell the LLM what library to use. Give it examples to follow. Write smaller files. There are no new principles - follow the ones that already exist.
Don’t leave a codebase’s maintainability to the weights of a model.

data.title: 150 years of Hans Christian Andersen
data.author: wholeness
data.article_summary: 《丑小鸭》是安徒生于1843年发表的童话，具有自传色彩。故事讲述了一只因丑陋而被排斥的鸭子，最终变成美丽天鹅的历程，反映了安徒生自己作为 outsider 最终获得认可的命运。安徒生出身贫寒，父亲是鞋匠，母亲是文盲，他童年孤独，喜欢自编戏剧和玩具剧院。尽管因外貌丑陋备受嘲笑，但他通过创作童话获得了成功。他的许多作品，如《坚定的锡兵》和《卖火柴的小女孩》，都反映了他对孤独与困苦的理解。安徒生的外貌和举止常引人侧目，其怪异行为可能源于发育障碍。他的人生如同童话，虽饱经艰辛，最终实现了非凡成就。

44739494.article_content:
There once was an ugly duckling, so despised by the other birds that he fled the farm to explore the wider world. But because of his very great ugliness he was taunted there too, until one day he caught his image reflected in a pond and he had turned into a beautiful swan.
The Ugly Duckling
, first published in 1843, was one of Hans Christian Andersen’s many autobiographical fairy tales: “It matters nothing if one is born in a duck-yard,” he wrote, “if one has lain in a swan’s egg.”
Andersen’s subject, from the start, was the outsider destined for greatness. “At school,” he recalled in
The Fairy Tale of My Life
, the third of his three memoirs, “I told the boys curious stories in which I was always the chief person, but was sometimes ridiculed for that.” His stories were miniature epics (
The Princess and the Pea
is 300 words long) and his characters, like the author himself, solitary figures of spiritual greatness for whom the world is a place of inexplicable cruelty. Other versions of Anderson’s life can be found in his first published fairy tale,
The Tinderbox,
in which a clever soldier discovers the magic formula for wealth and success;
The Steadfast Tin Soldier,
in which a one-legged, love-sick toy falls from a window, is swallowed by a fish, and then thrown into a stove where he melts into a heart-shaped lump; and
The Little Match Girl
, where a frozen, homeless child, on her last night on Earth, gazes through a window at a happy bourgeois family.
Had Anderson been as handsome as Danny Kaye, who played him in the Hollywood musical
Hans Christian Andersen
(1952), he would not have become a teller of tales. It was his fabulous ugliness that fuelled his ambition. “I shall have no success with my appearance,” he reflected, “so I make use of whatever is available.”
Everyone who met him remarked on his appearance. As a 20-year-old student in Copenhagen, he was described as “a lanky figure in a worn-out grey coat whose sleeves did not reach his emaciated wrists”. As a 40-year-old celebrity in a London drawing-room, he was described as “long, thin, fleshless, boneless… wriggling and bending like a lizard with a lantern-jawed, cadaverous visage”. He described himself in one of his poems as having a nose “as mighty as a cannon” and eyes as “tiny” as “green peas”. Edmund Gosse was “almost painfully struck… by the grotesque ugliness of his face and hands, and by his enormously long and swinging arms”. Anderson’s friend William Bloch also recalled his “out of proportion” arms and legs, together with his “broad and flat” hands, and “feet of such gigantic dimensions” that no one would ever steal his boots.
Added to this were what Bloch called Anderson’s “strange and bizarre” movements, and others noted his “ludicrous” manners and “obsequious contortions”, including deep theatrical bows. Heinrich Heine, the living writer Anderson most admired, mistook him for “a tailor” because of his “fawning servility”. If he sounds like a character invented by Charles Dickens, it is because Uriah Heep was modelled on Andersen, whom Dickens met in 1847. David Copperfield’s first sighting of Heep was “a cadaverous face” peering out of the round tower: “He had a way of writhing when he wanted to express enthusiasm, which was very ugly, the snaky twistings of his throat and body.” “If you’re an eel, sir,” counsels Betsey Trotwood, “conduct yourself like one. If you’re a man, control your limbs, sir!” In our own kinder age, we might diagnose Anderson with dyspraxia.
The life of Andersen was indeed the stuff of fairy tales. He was born in 1805 in a one-room cottage in the poorest part of Odense, a town on the Danish island of Funen rich in folk heritage. His father was a cobbler whose workshop was also in the cottage, and his mother was an illiterate washerwoman; his aunt ran a brothel, and his grandfather was insane. As a boy, Andersen watched the old man carve wooden figures with beasts’ heads, which he then gave to the village children. It was in the spinning room of the asylum where his grandmother was employed that he first heard the fairy tales that transfixed him, and when, on forest walks, his father told him tales from
The Arabian Nights
, Andersen knew he was destined to be another Scheherazade.
Andersen, a dreamy and effeminate only child, preferred his own company. His favourite pastime was the toy theatre made by his father, for which he wrote plays to be performed by the dolls whose clothes he designed and sewed. His first production was a tragedy taken from a song in
Pyramus and Thisbe
, the play within the play performed by the mechanicals in A
Midsummer Night’s Dream
. “Everyone was obliged to hear my play,” Anderson recalled in his first memoir,
The True Story of My Life
, written when he was 27 and not yet a household name. “It was a perfect treat for me to read it, and it never occurred to me that my audience might not experience the same pleasure in listening.” Anderson’s performances were mocked by the street boys

data.author: jandrewrogers
data.article_summary: Earthquake Event Page应用支持大多数现代浏览器，用户也可选择使用实时通知、订阅源和网络服务获取最新信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本东部海啸预警及其影响，包括不同地区海啸的实际影响、地震强度以及公众反应。

不同观点：
• **[decimalenough]** 提到日本东部海岸发布了海啸预警，预计海啸高达3米，并指出这与2011年福岛海啸同一地区。更新信息显示，实际海啸波浪较小，最高仅40厘米，可能不会造成重大损害。同时提供了日语和英语的直播链接。
• **[vasusen]** 提到其妻子因一个2025年日本地震预言的漫画而取消了前往日本的旅行，并调侃当前的海啸预警似乎验证了这一预言，尽管该预言曾引发过度恐慌和航班取消。
• **[yinser]** 认为此次地震规模非常大，可能会进入有史以来最大地震的前八名，并附上维基百科相关列表链接。
• **[dhx]** 引用了DART浮标观测到的水柱高度变化数据，指出在俄罗斯附近海域有显著变化。
• **[andsoitis]** 提供了美国西海岸、夏威夷和阿拉斯加的海啸预警链接，指出夏威夷和阿拉斯加处于警告状态，而美国西海岸则是“观察”状态。
• **[mordechai9000]** 关注俄罗斯彼得罗巴甫洛夫斯克的震害情况，引用了USGS的“严重”震动评估，并提到该地区过去几周有多次强震活动。
• **[user____name]** 批评了在灾难预警中争论海啸是否为“波浪”的无意义行为，暗示在紧急情况下讨论重点不当。
• **[bicx]** 指出俄罗斯该地区最近有大量地震活动，并持续收到地震警报。
• **[Kozmik1]** 提到中途岛和关岛的海啸波幅为3英尺（1米），引用了夏威夷州长Josh Green的信息。
• **[supportengineer]** 关心在夏威夷的家人的安全，担心瓦基基地区可能会被洪水袭击，并提到一些餐厅提前关闭。
• **[chasd00]** 在哥斯达黎加度假，提到其酒店海滩因海啸预警关闭，但通过直播摄像头未看到明显海啸影响。
• **[watkajtys]** 提供了地震及其周边地震活动的可视化链接，帮助理解地震影响。
• **[N19PEDL2]** 指出此次地震是地球上有记录以来的第六强地震。
• **[haunter]** 提到千叶有鲸鱼被冲上岸，附上了社交媒体链接。
• **[swader999]** 提供了关于地震的Dutchsinse覆盖视频链接，供进一步了解。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：当前海啸预警与2025年日本地震预言的关联性被调侃，但多数讨论集中在地震和海啸的实际影响及数据分析上。
• 数据引用：多个评论引用了实时数据、观测数据和官方预警链接，提供了较为全面的信息来源。
• 地区关注：讨论覆盖了日本、俄罗斯、美国夏威夷和阿拉斯加等多个地区的海啸预警和实际影响，显示出事件的跨国影响。

data.title: Supervised fine tuning on curated data is reinforcement learning
data.author: GabrielBianconi
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了监督微调（SFT）在精选数据上的应用，并将其与强化学习（RL）的理论和实践联系起来。作者指出，SFT 可以视为在稀疏奖励设置中最大化 RL 目标的下界，从而解释了其良好表现。基于此观点，作者提出了一种重要性加权微调（iw-SFT）变体，通过优化更紧的下界来提升性能。实验表明，iw-SFT 在处理大型语言模型和连续控制任务的策略训练时，表现可与更先进的 RL 算法相媲美，例如在 AIME 2024 数据集上达到了 66.7% 的成绩。文章提供了相关代码和详细实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用小型语言模型与大型语言模型性能对比的实验及其相关方法论的讨论

不同观点：
• anndvision认为，通过在高质量自动筛选的大模型输出上微调小型模型，可以在降低推理成本和时间的情况下，超越大型模型的性能。他们通过在多个基准测试（如BabyAI、Multi-Hop、τ-bench）上验证了这一结论，并计划发布更多实验结果。
• iandanforth质疑将此类优化问题视为强化学习（RL）是否有帮助。他认为RL是一种优化方法，关键在于其涉及代理在环境中多次决策的序列决策过程。如果缺乏这种特性，称之为RL并不恰当。
• henriquegodoy支持将AI视为系统中的模块化组件，而非代理。这种方法可以通过构建监测过程来降低成本，并通过提炼超大模型为小型模型实现。
• mandevil对两个独立研究者的研究表示好奇，询问其背景，是否为副项目。
• markisus指出公式（5）可能存在问题，认为中间期望值会因指示函数而出现许多零，从而可以人为调整成功阈值使中间期望接近零。
• stolencode以讽刺口吻评论学术界中发表论文多于实际工作的现象，暗示对实验结果的实际价值持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 实验方法的有效性和实用性受到关注，特别是成本和性能的权衡。
• 强化学习定义的适用性存在争议，反映出在方法论框架上的不同理解。
• 对研究项目背景的兴趣以及对实验细节和数学推导的质疑，显示出社区对透明度和可重复性的重视。
• 对学术研究和实际应用之间差距的批评，提示了对研究成果实际影响的反思。

Title:
Supervised Fine Tuning on Curated Data is Reinforcement Learning (and can be improved)
Authors:
Chongli Qin
,
Jost Tobias Springenberg
View a PDF of the paper titled Supervised Fine Tuning on Curated Data is Reinforcement Learning (and can be improved), by Chongli Qin and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Behavior Cloning (BC) on curated (or filtered) data is the predominant paradigm for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of large language models; as well as for imitation learning of control policies. Here, we draw on a connection between this successful strategy and the theory and practice of finding optimal policies via Reinforcement Learning (RL). Building on existing literature, we clarify that SFT can be understood as maximizing a lower bound on the RL objective in a sparse reward setting. Giving support to its often observed good performance. From this viewpoint, we realize that a small modification to SFT leads to an importance weighted variant that behaves closer to training with RL as it: i) optimizes a tighter bound to the RL objective and, ii) can improve performance compared to SFT on curated data. We refer to this variant as importance weighted supervised fine-tuning (iw-SFT). We show that it is easy to implement and can be further generalized to training with quality scored data. The resulting SFT variants are competitive with more advanced RL algorithms for large language models and for training policies in continuous control tasks. For example achieving 66.7% on the AIME 2024 dataset.

data.title: Attention is your scarcest resource
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者在管理工作和编程任务之间分配注意力的挑战，特别是在成为经理初期时由于分心于编程而导致管理不善。作者指出，知识工作者的产出与专注度密切相关，只有对某个任务投入50%以上的专注才能成为“超级明星”员工。为了保持专注，作者提出了几种策略：一是对工作结果有情感上的投入，二是单任务处理，避免同时处理多个任务，三是逃避不必要的义务以减少分心。通过这些策略，作者学会了更好地管理注意力，从而在重要任务上取得进展。最终，作者强调了专注对于高效工作的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：注意力的分配与管理工作生活平衡

不同观点：
• Simon_O_Rourke认为注意力是相对的，某些情况下分心是合理的，比如为了孩子。他批评了文章中提到的某些人为了职业发展而忽视家庭时间。
• baxtr提出注意力的花费等同于生命的花费，建议人们放下手机，享受生活。
• tossandthrow对文章标题立即做出反应，选择关闭网页去做更有意义的事情，暗示对文章主题的认同。
• dondraper36同意文章的前提，但作为ADHD患者，认为在工作受阻时不做其他事情是不现实的，特别是在大多数公司环境中。
• anyg表示自己倾向于“全有或全无”的做事方式，计划尝试时间盒管理法来改善注意力分配问题。
• uludag对文章中的一句话深有感触，认为自己无法控制情感投入，这种无力感影响了他的专注能力。
• amelius将互联网比作注意力的实际货币，暗示互联网对注意力的争夺。
• nikanj认为注意力是拥有充足其他资源的人的稀缺资源。
• tobyhinloopen指出AI编码虽然提高工作效率，但也减少了对每个项目的注意力投入，尽管如此，工作仍然能够完成。
• incognito124关注注意力的增加和情境切换的优化问题，认为这些能力可能可以通过某种方式提升。
• asplake作为管理者，认为注意力是最稀缺的资源，缺乏战略或操作背景是每个人的问题，两者是相互关联的。
• water9简单直接地指出时间是最稀缺的资源。
• lagrange77强烈反对广告和营销，认为它们试图强制窃取最稀缺的资源——注意力。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提及注意力与时间管理的关系，部分评论者如baxtr和water9强调时间与生命的关系，而tobyhinloopen和dondraper36则关注技术对注意力的影响和工作环境的实际限制。
• 争议的焦点在于注意力是否能够以及如何被有效管理和增加，特别是在现代工作环境和技术（如AI）的影响下。
• 广告和营销被部分评论者如lagrange77视为对注意力的不当争夺，这一外部因素在讨论中被提出作为影响注意力分配的重要因素。

44724216.article_content:
Like many people, I have most of my best ideas in the shower.
This is sometimes annoying: I could use more than one shower’s worth of good ideas a day, but I’d rather not end up as a shrivelled yet insightful prune. Mostly, though, shower ideas are the incentive that keeps me smelling okay, so I grudgingly accept the constraint.
The time when it was most constraining was the first time I became a manager. I only had a few reports, so managing them wasn’t a full-time job. But I was very bad at it, and so it
should have
been what I spent all my shower insights on.
Unfortunately, I was spending my non-management time on programming. And even if I tried to use my showers to think about my thorny and awkward people issues, my mind somehow always wandered off to tackle those nice, juicy software design problems instead.
Management Attempt #1 didn’t go very well; being distracted by programming, I made lots of embarrassing mistakes that made my reports’ lives harder, which in turn made me feel stressed and guilty. I ended up bouncing back to being an individual contributor after a few months.
That experience of mine resonates strongly with Byrne Hobart’s
observation about focus in knowledge work
:
The output of knowledge workers is extremely skewed based on focus. The productivity tiers seem to be:
<10% focused on the job at hand: meaningful risk of getting fired.
10-50% focus: âmeets expectations,â gets regular raises.
50%+ focus: superstar, 10x engineer, destined for greatness.
“50%+ focus” is roughly when something becomes
the top idea in your mind
. It’s when you start caring enough to think about it in the shower. It’s when you start habitually asking “how could this go faster?” It’s when you get
relentlessly resourceful
. It’s around when you start
annoying your coworkers and/or significant other
, although that part is avoidable with practice.
Most importantly, you can only be 50%+-focused on one thing at a time—or zero, in bad cases. That makes it critical to conserve your attention, so that you can spend it on what matters.
I’ve found a few different strategies that help me with this:
Care viscerally
It’s hard to recruit 50%+ of your brain to work on something just because you feel like you “should” do it. Your superego might listen to this newfangled “logic” and “reason” stuff, but the monkey-era parts of your brain can’t be fooled so easily. To be reliably able to focus on something, you need to be intuitively, emotionally invested in the outcome.
For me, that’s not automatic—for instance, even though
I’m incredibly excited about what Wave is doing
, my day-to-day motivation gets worse if I work remotely for too long without visiting our operations in Senegal. Unless I can periodically see for myself that people are using the things we’re building, it starts feeling a little bit fake, like the so-called “real world” is a simulation that I can only communicate with via Slack channels and
git push
.
Monotask
As a programmer, I tried to make sure that I was only ever working on one thing at a time. Even if I got stuck on that one thing—say I was blocked on waiting for a tech partner to give me API documentation—I’d let myself stay stuck instead of sliding off to work on something else.
In the short term, this made me less efficient, because I’d spend less time programming and more time staring vacantly at the ceiling. But if I stared vacantly for long enough, I’d eventually get mad enough to, e.g., reverse-engineer the partner’s API in a fit of rage. This resulted in me shipping my most important projects faster, hence getting
faster compounding growth
.
Evade obligations
As a manager, it became impossible to “only work on one thing:” there were too many small tasks and too many projects going on in parallel. But I have a similar principle: I can only have one
obligation to other people
. “Give advice on this project?” Whenever you want! “Review my 1,000-line change?” Only if review isn’t blocking you from shipping it. “Check in every so often to make sure this doesn’t go off the rails?” Sorry, I have to, uh, powder my nose. “Figure out what the process should be?” I’ll get back to you in a couple years. (The best process is no process, right?)
During Management Attempt #1, my programming project distracted me so much because other people cared a lot that I finished it—if I ever had to de-prioritize it, I would make those people sad. This made it take up my attention (by worrying about letting people down) even when I wasn’t working on it. Unfortunately, since management work comes in urgent bursts, I’d often end up in a situation where I had to delay either the programming or the management—i.e., choose between making two different sets of people sad—and in those cases it was very hard for me to control my focus.
Now that I’ve noticed this, I allow myself to contribute to multiple things in parallel, as long as they don’t tax my object permanence skills—if I totally forgot about this project today, wo

data.title: A Quantum Gravimeter for GPS Backup
data.author: purpleko
data.article_summary: 澳大利亚船只使用全球首台海洋量子双重力仪导航设备，在没有GPS的情况下连续航行六天。该设备由Q-CTRL公司开发，旨在GPS不可用或不可信时提供可靠的导航解决方案。量子重力仪通过测量地球重力场的微小变化帮助船只精确定位，展示了未来替代GPS的潜力。这一技术对国防和民用航海具有重要意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子惯性传感器及其作为GPS替代品的可行性

不同观点：
• **jauntywundrkind**：对X-37B任务中的量子惯性传感器和激光通信技术表示兴趣。他提到磁场传感可能会随时间变化，但对实际效果持观望态度，认为需要通过实验验证。

• **bob1029**：认为像BPS（精准时间传输技术）这样的方法可能更可行，并提供了相关技术文献支持其观点。

• **bravesoul2**：提出使用天体（如太阳、星座或月亮）、时间及指南针确定位置的传统方法，并询问这种方法在有良好仪器和计算机辅助下是否可以作为可靠的备用方案。同时指出夜间和阴天条件下的局限性。

• **rich_sasha**：质疑精确测量重力波动后的实际应用，询问是否存在重力波动地图用于对比，并探讨了重力波动是否受地形（如山脉、湖泊）影响。

• **amelius**：关注量子惯性传感器的输出形式，询问其是否能够测量不同方向的重力，还是仅生成单一的标量值。

• **tamimio**：关心天气条件（如云、暴雨、飓风等）对量子惯性传感器的影响，引用Biercuk的话指出重力无法被伪造，但对天气因素的影响表示关注。

补充讨论：

data.title: New DNA Map of the Pistachio Could Create Better Varieties
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员生成了最全面的开心果基因组序列，为培育更优质、更营养的品种提供了可能。该序列比以往的基因图谱更加精确，有助于农民更可持续地管理作物，尤其是在应对气候变化带来的挑战时。研究详细描述了开心果生长的四个关键阶段，从开花到收获，帮助农民更好地决策如何浇水和收获，以避免虫害和真菌感染。此外，研究还揭示了影响开心果营养价值的基因和途径，为培育更具营养的品种奠定了基础。这项研究由加州开心果研究委员会等机构资助。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： pistachios作为农作物的优点及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• AngryData认为，pistachios是一种适合在干旱地区种植的优秀植物。它们相比其他作物需水量少，并且能够使用微咸/盐碱水，这使得在加州等沿海地区种植pistachios更加经济和简便，无需完全依赖淡水资源。
• ggm则更关注pistachios在消费过程中出现的问题，特别是未开口的壳果在烘烤后仍然难以打开，影响了食用体验。他还提到pistachios带来的即时满足感可能导致过量食用，并引用《太空商人》中的概念，暗示这种高满足感食品可能导致不健康的消费习惯。

补充讨论：
• AngryData的论据集中在pistachios的农业优势，特别是其节水特性和适应盐碱环境的能力，这些特性使得pistachios在干旱和沿海地区具有很高的种植价值。
• ggm的评论虽然提到pistachios的农业特性，但更多关注消费者角度，尤其是食用pistachios时遇到的实际问题（如壳果不易打开）和潜在的健康风险（如过量食用导致的高血压）。他还通过引用文学作品《太空商人》来加强其对pistachios消费吸引力的批评。
• 争议的焦点在于pistachios的消费体验和健康影响。AngryData强调其农业优势，而ggm则担心消费者可能因pistachios的强烈满足感而过度消费，从而引发健康问题。

总结来看，讨论的核心在于pistachios的种植优势与消费体验、健康影响之间的平衡。

Cracking the Code of Pistachio Genetics
New DNA Map Could Lead to More Nutritious, Sustainable Nuts
by
Amy Quinton
March 20, 2025
News
Researchers have generated the most comprehensive genome sequence of the pistachio, allowing plant breeders to create better varieties. (Bárbara Blanco-Ulate / UC Davis)
California produces 99% of the nation’s pistachios, generating nearly $3 billion in economic value in the state. But pistachios have been slightly understudied in part because of the lack of a high-quality map of their DNA. University of California, Davis, researchers have now generated the most comprehensive genome sequence of the pistachio, allowing plant breeders to create better — perhaps more nutritious — varieties. They’ve also detailed how pistachio nuts develop, which will help farmers manage their crop more sustainably.
New Phytologist published
the study
today.
Scientists have sequenced the DNA of pistachios before, but co-corresponding author J. Grey Monroe, an assistant professor with the Department of Plant Sciences, said this new genetic map is vastly more detailed and accurate.
“The improvement in accuracy of the new reference genome is like going from a hand-drawn map of a landscape to a satellite image from Google Earth,” he said.
Monroe and the research team sequenced the genome of the Kerman cultivar, the most common pistachio variety grown in California.
Climate change challenges pistachio yields
Pistachio trees are resilient to drought and salinity, but they require cold winters to flower properly. As climate change brings warmer winters, growers need new pistachio varieties that can thrive in higher temperatures. Warm winters, combined with the dissipation of fogs that cool California’s Central Valley, have caused significant losses for pistachio growers.
Pistachios just beginning to develop. Researchers have detailed how pistachio nuts develop, which could allow farmers to manage their crops more sustainably. (Bárbara Blanco-Ulate / UC Davis)
Given that establishing a pistachio tree requires a commitment of up to 50 years, researchers said California growers are understandably concerned about the impacts of climate change on their crops.
A nutty development
The study also identifies four key stages of nut growth from flower to harvest, providing a complete physiological assessment, including shell hardening and kernel growth.
“Knowing how the nut changes through development will help farmers make better decisions, like when to water their trees, leading to more sustainable pistachio production,” said co-corresponding author Bárbara Blanco-Ulate, an associate professor with the Department of Plant Sciences.
Researchers detailed four stages of the pistachio’s development, which could allow farmers to manage their crops more sustainably. (Bárbara Blanco-Ulate/UC Davis)
A more accurate assessment of its development could also help provide growers better strategies for harvest and avoid issues such as insect damage and fungal infections.
Blanco-Ulate said it was important to also detail not just the physical changes of the pistachios, but also the genetic and molecular drivers of those characteristics. The genomic sequence includes precedent-setting information on how different genes behave in nuts over the growing season.
Nutritious nut
Pistachios have always been a nutritious food, but researchers have now discovered the genes and pathways that influence their nutritional value. This includes insights into how protein and unsaturated fatty acids accumulate, which is crucial for both their shelf life and dietary benefits.
Stage IV of the pistachio’s development, when its shell begins to develop a red color. (Adrian Sbodio / UC Davis)
“We’re getting information about how all these nutritional characteristics are gained in pistachios and how we can improve that from a management perspective,” said Blanco-Ulate.
This understanding could help scientists breed more nutritional pistachios in the future.
The first authors of the paper are Jaclyn Adaskaveg and Chaehee Lee of UC Davis. Other UC Davis authors include Yiduo Wei, Fangyi Wang, Saskia D. Mesquida-Pesci, Matthew Davis, Louise Ferguson, Giulia Marino, Patrick J. Brown, Georgia Drakakaki, Selina Wang and Filipa S. Grilo.
Research was funded by the California Pistachio Research Board, the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture and the Foundation for Food and Agricultural Research.

data.title: RIP Shunsaku Tamiya, the man who made plastic model kits a global obsession
data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: 日本知名模型制造商田宫（Tamiya）的前董事长田宫俊作于7月18日去世，享年90岁。他带领公司从运输和木材业务转型为生产高精度塑料模型、遥控车和迷你四驱车，推动了模型行业向塑料模型的转变。田宫俊作邀请其兄弟设计了公司标志性的“双星”logo，并通过独特的“白盒”包装设计提升了品牌辨识度。他为追求精确，曾购入保时捷911并拆解以完善模型细节。2018年，他荣获日本媒体艺术节的终身成就奖，以表彰其对模型行业的贡献。他的创新和追求卓越的精神对模型爱好者产生了深远影响。

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun：认为塑料模型制作是一个充满乐趣的爱好，尤其是在年轻时通过拼装模型培养了空间感和设计思维。但对这一爱好逐渐衰落感到遗憾，因为现代似乎更加注重在线活动，传统爱好不再流行。

• kawsper：指出Tamiya的影响已扩展到其他爱好领域，如airsoft和无人机中使用的Tamiya连接器。
• mirkodrummer：怀念与父亲一起制作迷你四驱车的经历，认为这种体验对年轻人有教育意义。
• Aeolun：分享了与儿子及其朋友一起制作Tamiya车的愉快经历，并对店铺提供工具和赛道的服务表示赞赏。
• esafak：提到制作模型和绘画战锤40K微缩模型对精细运动技能的提升作用。

补充讨论：
• kkylin：指出RC车技术多年来似乎没有显著变化，并对现代是否有新的技术融入这一爱好表示疑问，同时怀念自己青少年时期从模型制作中学到的机械工程知识。

争议焦点：
• 传统模型爱好是否在现代社会中逐渐衰落，以及现代模型的简单化和品牌化趋势是否削弱了其教育和艺术价值。

44728188.article_content:
Shunsaku Tamiya, former president and chairman of Tamiya, Inc., passed away on July 18. His death was announced on July 21, with funeral services attended by close family and friends. Mr Tamiya led the transformation of Tamiya into a world-renowned manufacturer of high-precision plastic model kits, radio control vehicles, and motorized Mini 4WD racers.
He joined the company founded by his father originally as a transport firm, and switched to supplying lumber after the war. That brought about an expansion into wooden models, primarily of ships and planes. After a fire destroyed the company’s lumber supply, it focused primarily on the models.
Not long after, plastic technology improved and began taking over the model kit market. Shunsuke Tamiya spearheaded the shift to
puramo
(a portmanteau of “plastic” and “model”) and in the process changed the industry. He helped fuel enthusiasm for cars, as well as other types of transportation, for generations of children and adults alike.
Shunsaku Tamiya was responsible for creating Tamiya’s signature branding and reputation for quality. He invited his brother Masao to create the “twin stars” logo and hired illustrators to create the “white box” look that made Tamiya stand out in sharp contrast to the box art of other model makers.
Most of all, he was the driving force in the unmatched precision Tamiya kits have come to be celebrated for. Famously, while creating the model kit for the 1976 Porsche 934 Turbo RSR, Tamiya-san sent his designers to Porsche’s Zuffenhausen factory several times to get the measurements and details just right. However, despite repeated trips there were still doubts about the kit’s accuracy. So Tamiya bought a Porsche 911 and completely disassembled it to get every detail correct. Eventually, the car was put back together, and Shunsaku Tamiya personally ferried Jody Scheckter and his wife to the 1976 Japan Grand Prix in it.
In 2018 Shunsaku Tamiya was given a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Japan Media Arts Festival for his contributions to the hobby industry. His contributions to the imaginations of petrolheads, however, will live on for many more years to come. Shunsaku Tamiya was 90 years old.

• JKCalhoun：认为塑料模型制作是一个充满乐趣的爱好，尤其是在年轻时通过拼装模型培养了空间感和设计思维。但对这一爱好逐渐衰落感到遗憾，因为现代似乎更加注重在线活动，传统爱好不再流行。
• louthy：分享了自己在80年代玩Tamiya遥控车的经历，尽管改造导致车辆损坏，但回忆中仍充满乐趣。
• radpanda：提到Tamiya为了模型精准度而购买真车进行拆解的故事，并对这种追求极致的精神表示钦佩，同时对这种行为是否与税务有关表示调侃。
• firefax：对模型的艺术性和技能要求表示肯定，但也指出由于个人在精细操作上的困难，无法完全参与其中。同时担忧现代模型的简单化和品牌化趋势。
• billforsternz：对多个国家制造商持续生产经典飞机模型的现象感到有趣，并好奇是否存在行业内知名的工匠。
• spankibalt：提到在东德时期对模型和设计产生的兴趣，并表达对模型盒子艺术的喜爱。
• hydrogen7800：分享了自己对Tamiya RC车的技术细节和改装经验，认为虽然存在设计缺陷，但模型车仍有其独特的吸引力。
• kawsper：指出Tamiya的影响已扩展到其他爱好领域，如airsoft和无人机中使用的Tamiya连接器。
• mirkodrummer：怀念与父亲一起制作迷你四驱车的经历，认为这种体验对年轻人有教育意义。
• Aeolun：分享了与儿子及其朋友一起制作Tamiya车的愉快经历，并对店铺提供工具和赛道的服务表示赞赏。
• esafak：提到制作模型和绘画战锤40K微缩模型对精细运动技能的提升作用。

补充讨论：
• kkylin：指出RC车技术多年来似乎没有显著变化，并对现代是否有新的技术融入这一爱好表示疑问，同时怀念自己青少年时期从模型制作中学到的机械工程知识。

争议焦点：
• 传统模型爱好是否在现代社会中逐渐衰落，以及现代模型的简单化和品牌化趋势是否削弱了其教育和艺术价值。

data.title: Zuckerberg: 'superintelligence is now in sight' as Meta lavishes billions on AI
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary: Meta首席执行官马克·扎克伯格在2025年7月表示，公司致力于开发“超级智能”，并已投入巨资提升人工智能（AI）能力。尽管“超级智能”的具体定义尚未明确，扎克伯格称其将带来新的安全问题，并强调Meta的目标是将个人超级智能带给所有人，而不仅仅是用于生产力或工作自动化。尽管Meta的巨额支出引发投资者关注，但公司第二季度财报超出华尔街预期，营收达475.2亿美元，每股收益7.14美元，推动股价大涨。Meta预计2025年总支出将达1140亿至1180亿美元，其中大部分用于AI研发。投资者关注其AI投资是否能带来持续的现金流回报。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）和大型语言模型（LLM）的未来发展及其实际能力

不同观点：
• [richardatlarge] 认为某些AI领域的领军人物或公司所做的预测不可靠，甚至可以作为反向指标来 betting against（下注反对）。他暗示这些预测可能只是为了维护其公司或帝国的利益，且对未来的预见有限，仅能看到其帝国的必然衰落。

• [nehal3m] 对当前LLM的能力持怀疑态度，认为尽管这些技术能完成一些有用的任务，但它们不能被称为真正的“智能”。他还批评科技行业的领导者（如Zuckerberg等）为了维持高股价，继续假装AI处于增长市场的初期阶段，实际上是在推动一场大规模的炒作。

• [_rm] 对AI能力的发展曲线提出疑问，并希望了解其他人是否认为AI能力会像“曲棍球杆”形状一样，随着时间推移出现爆发式增长。他个人感觉AI工具的能力已经趋于饱和，未来的效用可能会呈现指数级的衰减，而不是增长。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI和LLM技术是否真正具备“智能”，以及这些技术未来的发展潜力。一部分人认为当前的AI技术被过度炒作，其实际能力有限，而另一些人则对AI未来能力的指数级增长持怀疑态度，认为其效用会逐渐减弱。

• 讨论中还涉及对科技行业领导者动机的质疑，认为他们可能出于经济利益而夸大AI的潜力，从而推动市场炒作。

• 不同观点之间的讨论关系表现为对AI现状和发展前景的不同判断，以及对行业领导者动机和市场行为的批评。

Mark Zuckerberg at the Chase Center in San Francisco, September 2024.
Photograph: Laure Andrillon/Reuters
View image in fullscreen
Mark Zuckerberg at the Chase Center in San Francisco, September 2024.
Photograph: Laure Andrillon/Reuters
Technology
Zuckerberg claims ‘superintelligence is now in sight’ as Meta lavishes billions on AI
In advance of Meta’s quarterly earnings report, CEO says his company aims to bring powerful AI into the lives of millions
Johana Bhuiyan
Wed 30 Jul 2025 18.32 EDT
First published on Wed 30 Jul 2025 15.07 EDT
Share
Whether it’s poaching top talent away from competitors, acquiring AI startups or proclaiming that it will build data centers the size of Manhattan,
Meta
has been on a spending spree to boost its artificial intelligence capabilities for months now.
The massive splurge is paying off, according to Meta’s chief executive. In a new
memo
posted on Wednesday ahead of the company’s quarterly earnings report, Mark Zuckerberg, describes his ambitions for developing what he calls “superintelligence”.
“Over the last few months we have begun to see glimpses of our AI systems improving themselves,” Zuckerberg wrote. “The improvement is slow for now, but undeniable. Developing superintelligence is now in sight.”
Wall Street investors are happy with the expensive course Zuckerberg is charting. After the company reported better-than-expected financial results for yet another quarter, its stock soared by double digits.
Though Zuckerberg did not provide any details of what would qualify as “superintelligence” versus standard artificial intelligence, he did say that it would pose “novel safety concerns”.
“We’ll need to be rigorous about mitigating these risks and careful about what we choose to open source,” he wrote.
Zuckerberg wrote that the company differs from other AI firms in that Meta aims to bring “personal superintelligence to everyone”. Other companies are focused on primarily using “superintelligence” for productivity and to automate “all valuable work”, he wrote.
“The rest of this decade seems likely to be the decisive period for determining the path this technology will take, and whether superintelligence will be a tool for personal empowerment or a force focused on replacing large swaths of society,” he wrote.
Investors want to know: does AI mean cashflow?
Investors are looking for signs that the parent company of WhatsApp,
Instagram
and Facebook is spending its billions efficiently. The social media company reported its second quarter earnings on Wednesday after the close of the New York stock exchange and beat investor expectations yet again sending stocks soaring 10%. Analysts expect Meta will have to answer questions about whether the revenue the company is bringing in will help offset the hundreds of billions the firm is spending on recruiting and infrastructure, collectively known as capital expenditure.
“AI-driven investments into Meta’s advertising business continue to pay off, bolstering its revenue as the company pours billions of dollars into AI ambitions like superintelligence,” said Minda Smiley, a senior analyst at Emarketer. “But Meta’s exorbitant spending on its AI visions will continue to draw questions and scrutiny from investors who are eager to see returns.”
Meta reported $7.14 in earnings per share (EPS) on $47.52bn in revenue, surpassing Wall Street expectations of $5.92 in earnings per share on $44.8bn in revenue. This quarter is the latest in the company’s multiple-quarter streak of exceeding Wall Street’s financial expectations despite enormous spending on AI.
The company also said it expects to bring in $47.5bn to 50.5bn in revenue in the third quarter of 2025.
Zuckerberg provided few tangible updates in the memo, but one thing is clear: getting to this so-called higher level of intelligence will require a great deal of capital. Meta reported that the total costs and expenditures for the second quarter of 2025 came in at $27.07bn – up 12% year over year. Capital expenditures for the quarter were $17.01bn.
The company also provided updated guidance on how much the firm expects to spend in the next few months. Meta said it expected to spend between $114bn and $118bn in total expenses in 2025 – a slight adjustment from its previous projection of between $113bn and $118bn. Of that, Meta said it expected its capital expenditures to amount to somewhere in the range of $66bn and $72bn. The company previously predicted it would spend between $64bn and $72bn which was increased from an even earlier prediction of $60bn to $65bn.

data.title: ACM Transitions to Full Open Access
data.author: pcvarmint
data.article_summary: ACM正在向全面开放获取（Open Access, OA）模式转型，计划在2025年底实现所有研究内容的自由获取。这一举措旨在消除获取和发表研究的障碍，促进计算研究的发展。ACM的开放获取框架名为“ACM Open”，为机构提供无限制的OA出版，且不收取文章处理费（APCs）。定价基于机构过去三年的出版量，确保公平和可预测。参与机构还将获得ACM数字图书馆的高级版访问权，包括超过80万篇研究文章和多种研究工具。自2026年起，ACM数字图书馆将提供高级和基本两种访问选项，高级版包括扩展的文献检索、AI辅助搜索和研究影响分析等功能。APC费用从700美元到1800美元不等，具体取决于文章类型和作者身份。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术出版的开放获取、费用及版权许可问题

不同观点：
• lsuresh认为USENIX会议是理想的发表平台，因为其帮助组织会议，所有论文都开放获取，无需登录即可下载。这种模式让研究者可以专注于提交论文和参与程序委员会，而不必依赖大量志愿者。

• raphaelmo则更倾向于LIPIcs系统，该系统由德国支持，提供现代化的论文提交接口，且相比USENIX的开放获取费用更低。

• rezmason以幽默的方式表达对大量待读文献的感慨，并提议成立“ACM酷论文俱乐部”。

• kragen赞赏ACM向开放获取的转变，但质疑其具体的许可条款，指出根据柏林宣言的定义，开放获取应包括授权的自由使用和分发权，而ACM的现行政策下，个人上传或分享论文仍可能面临版权诉讼风险。

• subharmonicon表示因ACM拒绝支持开放获取，已取消会员资格。

• bubblethink批评出版费用高昂，指出费用范围在700至1800美元之间。

• throwaway81523对ACM开放获取的具体实施细节表示困惑，特别是关于已有文章是否仍将付费访问，以及机构与个人访问权限的区别。

• PaulHoule简单表达了对ACM开放获取进展的积极看法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于开放获取的定义和实施细节。kragen强调根据柏林宣言，开放获取应包括特定的版权许可，而ACM的现行政策在这方面存在不足。

• 不同平台和系统的比较，如USENIX和LIPIcs，涉及组织方式、费用及用户体验等方面。

• 费用问题也是讨论的核心之一，特别是出版费用的高昂以及机构和个人访问权限的复杂性，引发了对现行学术出版模式的质疑。

• 总体来看，评论者对开放获取的支持态度明确，但对具体实施和费用结构存在不同程度的批评和困惑。

44725966.article_content:
Open Access Publication & ACM
ACM's Transition to Full Open Access: A New Era for Computing Research
For more than seven decades, ACM has played a pivotal role in advancing computing research, fostering collaboration, and disseminating knowledge through its world-class Digital Library, influential publications, and premier conferences.
In a significant step to broadening access to computing research, ACM is transitioning to a fully Open Access (OA) publishing model by the end of 2025. This bold move marks a pivotal moment in making all ACM research content freely available and removing barriers to discovery and innovation.
ACM's journey towards Open Access has been a carefully considered, phased approach, ensuring the long-term sustainability of its publications program and the various educational, diversity, public policy, and community recognition initiatives it supports.
The move to Open Access is not just a change in policy, but a reflection of ACM's commitment to its community, where the goal is to remove barriers to publishing and accessing vital research, and accelerating the pace of discovery and innovation.
ACM’s approach to Open Access is centered on 2 key elements:
1. ACM Open – A Sustainable Open Access Framework for Institutions
ACM Open is a unique and innovative take on the Read & Publish model, offering institutions a seamless way to support Open Access publishing. For academic or research institutions, pricing is based on an institution’s publishing output, averaged over the previous three years, and remains fixed for the duration of the agreement. This approach ensures predictability in budgeting while providing unlimited Open Access publishing and full read access to ACM content.
Key Benefits of ACM Open:
Unlimited Open Access Publishing
Corresponding authors from participating institutions can publish an unlimited number of Open Access articles without Article Processing Charges (APCs).
Fair and Predictable Pricing
ACM Open’s fixed term annual price, based on an academic or research institution’s historical publishing activity, ensures transparency and budget stability. This pricing model helps institutions manage costs effectively while supporting Open Access publishing. For corporate pricing,
please refer here
. For government pricing,
please refer here
.
Premium Digital Library Access
Institutions subscribing to ACM Open receive full access to the Premium version of the ACM Digital Library, providing their users with unrestricted access to over 800,000 ACM published research articles, the ACM Guide to Computing Literature (which indexes more than 6,500 3rd party publishers with direct links to the content), advanced tools, and exclusive features.
2. ACM Digital Library – A Tailored Approach to Access and Engagement
ACM is introducing
Premium and Basic
access options for the ACM Digital Library in
January 2026
, supporting a sustainable approach to Open Access. Institutions that subscribe to ACM Open will automatically receive full Premium access. A stand-alone Digital Library Premium subscription will also be available, providing continued access to critical resources and tools that support world-class computing research.
The Premium ACM Digital Library Experience
Premium
access enables institutions to fully leverage ACM content, providing deeper insights, seamless workflows, and richer collaboration opportunities for their users.
Premium
features include:
Access to the ACM Guide to Computing Literature,
expanding research beyond ACM content for a broader view of computing research.
Advanced research tools,
including AI-assisted search, bulk downloads, and citation management, to streamline discovery and workflow.
Comprehensive research insights,
including article usage metrics, citation trends, and Altmetric tracking to measure research impact.

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI设计中“副驾驶”（copilot）和“平视显示器”（HUD）两种不同的隐喻。作者引用1992年研究者Mark Weiser的观点，批评了将AI视为“副驾驶”的思路，主张设计应让计算机自然融入背景，成为人的延伸，而非引人注意的助手。文章以现代飞机的HUD为例，说明HUD能让用户自然获得更多信息，如同拥有“魔法眼睛”，而不需与系统对话。作者认为，诸如拼写检查和自定义调试器等功能，就是软件中的HUD，它们在不打扰用户的情况下增强人类感知。文章最后指出，HUD和副驾驶各有优劣，设计者应根据具体情境选择适合的AI形式，在日常任务中可使用副驾驶，而在追求卓越结果时，则应赋予专家新的“超能力”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI在编程和人类-AI交互中的不同形式和界面设计的讨论，包括Copilot与HUD的比较、AI在不同场景下的最佳界面设计以及相关技术实现的争议。

不同观点：
• **Kevinphy**：通过日本动漫《Future GPX Cyber Formula》类比Copilot与HUD的区别。动漫中Asurada赛车代表Copilot，提供情感支持和战术分析；而对手的赛车则类似HUD，强调冷数据和无情感连接，反映了AI交互中的不同哲学和权衡。
• **Furyofantares**：建议在编码中引入热力图来标识代码中的潜在错误或问题，通过颜色提示开发者可能的错误，从而提升代码质量。
• **Cadamsdotcom**：提出实时生成测试的设想，即在编码时自动生成并运行测试，实时反馈结果。这种方法可以帮助开发者动态调整代码，并可用于传统TDD（测试驱动开发）的逆向操作。
• **Piker**：认为Copilot在某些情况下增加了编码延迟，不如特定工具（如`rust_analyzer`）有用。同时指出AI在辅助策略和教学方面有价值，但在复杂项目中的“类型预测”功能有限。
• **Sothatsit**：提出AI生成复杂可视化工具的用例，例如在调试内存泄漏时，通过可视化帮助识别问题，并提到Jonathan Blow的工具作为参考。

补充讨论：
• **_jab**：认为Copilot的核心功能——代码补全，实际上已经是HUD的一种形式，并通过具体例子说明这种体验的优点。
• **Hi_hi**：讨论了AI在处理和总结信息方面的作用，提出未来可能通过单一聊天界面获取信息，从而减少对传统网站和 dashboard 的依赖。
• **Ravila4**：指出HUD未广泛应用的一个原因是当前屏幕显示媒介的限制，提出VR/AR可能是AI HUD的理想应用场景，并强调这种技术在物理任务中的潜力。
• **Kn81198**：提到Bret Victor关于减少反馈延迟的原则，并指出其与HUD设计理念的相似性，强调更快迭代周期对创造性工作的帮助。
• **Afro88**：对HUD展示数据的准确性提出质疑，询问如何处理HUD中的错误信息，建议为每个元素提供来源按钮。
• **Thinkingemote**：强调HUD需要配合实际控制（如按钮、拨盘），而不仅仅是视觉信息展示，类似飞行员在驾驶舱中的操作。
• **Benjaminwootton**：提出第三种模型，即后台自主运行的AI，智能检测并推送总结和建议，特别适用于需要监控大量客户和情况的业务环境。
• **Keyle**：认为自动补全功能已经是HUD的一种形式，并指出AI应与人类“并肩作战”，而不是对立，最终目标是AI无需互动即可执行人类指令。
• **Ankit219**：讨论模型的可靠性和聊天作为主要交互媒介的局限性，指出在HUD中展示信息前需要更高的准确性，而在Copilot中人类可以参与校正。

争议焦点：
• HUD与Copilot在不同场景下的优劣对比，特别是信息准确性和用户体验的权衡。
• AI在实时反馈和自主运行中的技术实现和实际应用价值。
• 不同界面设计（如VR/AR、传统屏幕、物理控制）在AI交互中的适用性和前景。

44705445.article_content:
July 2025
Enough AI copilots! We need AI HUDs
In my opinion, one of the best critiques of modern AI design comes from
a 1992 talk
by the researcher
Mark Weiser
where he ranted against “copilot” as a metaphor for AI.
This was 33 years ago, but it’s still incredibly relevant for anyone designing with AI.
Weiser’s rant
Weiser was speaking at an
MIT Media Lab event
on “interface agents”. They were grappling with many of the same issues we’re discussing in 2025: how to make a personal assistant that automates tasks for you and knows your full context. They even had a human “butler” on stage representing an AI agent.
Everyone was super excited about this… except Weiser. He was opposed to the whole idea of agents! He gave this example: how should a computer help you fly a plane and avoid collisions?
The agentic option is a “copilot” — a virtual human who you talk with to get help flying the plane.
If you’re about to run into another plane it might yell at you “collision, go right and down!”
Weiser offered a different option:
design the cockpit so that the human pilot is naturally aware of their surroundings.
In his words: “You’ll no more run into another airplane than you would try to walk through a wall.”
Weiser’s goal was an “invisible computer"—not an assistant that grabs your attention, but a computer that fades into the background and becomes "an extension of [your] body”.
Weiser’s 1992 slide on airplane interfaces
HUDs
There’s a tool in modern planes that I think nicely illustrates Weiser’s philosophy:
the Head-Up Display (HUD), which overlays flight info like the horizon and altitude on a transparent display directly in the pilot’s field of view.
A HUD feels completely different from a copilot! You don’t talk to it. It’s literally part invisible—you just become naturally aware of more things, as if you had magic eyes.
Designing HUDs
OK enough analogies. What might a HUD feel like in modern software design?
One familiar example is spellcheck. Think about it:
spellcheck isn’t designed as a “virtual collaborator” talking to you about your spelling.
It just instantly adds red squigglies when you misspell something! You now have a new sense you didn’t have before. It’s a HUD.
(This example comes from Jeffrey Heer’s excellent
Agency plus Automation
paper. We may not consider spellcheck an AI feature today, but it’s still a fuzzy algorithm under the hood.)
Spellcheck makes you aware of misspelled words without an “assistant” interface.
Here’s another personal example from AI coding. Let’s say you want to fix a bug. The obvious “copilot” way is to open an agent chat and ask it to do the fix.
But there’s another approach I’ve found more powerful at times:
use AI to build a custom debugger UI which visualizes the behavior of my program!
In one example, I
built a hacker-themed debug view of a Prolog interpreter
.
With the debugger, I have a HUD! I have new senses, I can see how my program runs. The HUD extends beyond the narrow task of fixing the bug. I can ambiently build up my own understanding, spotting new problems and opportunities.
Both the spellchecker and custom debuggers show that automation / “virtual assistant” isn’t the only possible UI. We can instead use tech to build better HUDs that enhance our human senses.
Tradeoffs
I don’t believe HUDs are universally better than copilots! But I do believe
anyone serious about designing for AI should consider non-copilot form factors that more directly extend the human mind.
So when should we use one or the other? I think it’s quite tricky to answer that, but we can try to use the airplane analogy for some intuition:
When pilots just want the plane to fly straight and level, they fully delegate that task to an autopilot, which is close to a “virtual copilot”. But if the plane just hit a flock of birds and needs to land in the Hudson, the pilot is going to take manual control, and we better hope they have great instruments that help them understand the situation.
In other words: routine predictable work might make sense to delegate to a virtual copilot / assistant. But when you’re shooting for extraordinary outcomes, perhaps the best bet is to equip human experts with new superpowers.
Further reading
A nice discussion of one approach to this idea can be found in
Using Artificial Intelligence to Augment Human Intelligence
by Michael Nielsen and Shan Carter.
A more cryptic take on the same topic:
Is chat a good UI for AI? A Socratic dialogue
A discussion of how the the HUD philosophy intersects with on-demand software creation:
Malleable software in the age of LLMs
